summary: Tested admin alias login normalization and KYC gating across backend + frontend. Admin aliases map to canonical admin and bypass pre-KYC gates; non-admin pre-KYC restrictions remain. One critical CORS preflight credential header issue persists on public endpoint.

critical.issue: Public preflight response still omits Access-Control-Allow-Credentials header (expected true for credentialed auth flows).

issues: Several secondary texts use very low-contrast gray on dark backgrounds (e.g., #333/#444 tones), reducing readability.

action_items: Fix credentialed CORS preflight behavior for /api/auth/login at preview/public edge so Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true is consistently returned.
Optionally improve low-contrast secondary text colors in dark UI sections for accessibility/readability.
critical_code_review_comments: CORS middleware in app sets credentials correctly, but public preflight still fails expected headers, suggesting ingress/edge interception mismatch.
Auth alias canonicalization and admin KYC override path are now consistent across login, /me, and /refresh responses.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression file covers: alias->canonical admin login, admin kyc contract in /auth/me and /auth/refresh, httpOnly auth cookies, brute-force lockout threshold, and non-admin KYC contract sanity. Frontend browser run verified admin alias has no pre-kyc gates on Home/More and unverified non-admin still sees both gates.
rca of the issue: Repro: send OPTIONS to public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL/api/auth/login with Origin + Access-Control-Request-* headers. Result: 200/204 without access-control-allow-credentials. App middleware config includes credentialed CORS, so likely upstream edge/ingress preflight handling is overriding or short-circuiting response headers before app middleware response reaches client.
